name: Floating storage and regasification units (FSRU)
principle: A ship with LNG tanks and onboard vaporisers is moored at a jetty or buoy. LNG from carriers is transferred ship to ship, stored, pumped to pressure and vaporised with seawater or a closed loop, then sent to shore through a high-pressure arm or pipeline. NETL's import terminal model uses open rack vaporisers, which serve about all Asian and about 60% of European terminals.

process_steps.name: Gas send-out
equipment: HP gas arm or subsea pipeline

performance.basis: NETL import terminal model (open rack vaporisers)

source.note: NETL, Life Cycle GHG Perspective on Exporting LNG from the United States: 2019 Update, DOE/NETL-2019/2041, 12 September 2019, Exhibits 5-7 and 5-11, Appendix B

performance.basis: Excelerate newbuild at HHI, 170,000 m3 storage, delivery June 2026

reference_plants.name: Excelerate newbuild FSRU (Hyundai Heavy Industries)
reference_plants.capacity: 170,000 m3 storage, 1,000 MMscf/d send-out; fleet of 11 FSRUs operating or building

advantages: Faster and cheaper than onshore terminals
limitations: Limited storage compared with onshore tanks
Seawater vaporisers raise environmental permitting issues

sources.note: NETL, Life Cycle GHG Perspective on Exporting LNG from the United States: 2019 Update, DOE/NETL-2019/2041, 12 September 2019, Exhibits 5-7 and 5-11, Appendix B
